proposals.action: Append learned preference: '- 2026-07-26: treat US-administration self-characterizations as an unreliable narrator - do not relay the claim flat; attribute/quote the loaded word AND supply the missing legal or factual context the administration omits.' Extends the 2026-07-19 impartiality line from attribution to actively adding skeptical context.
proposals.evidence: 2x downvotes with written reasons on DISTINCT news stories this window, same escalating theme: news 2026-07-20 Iran 'final' night -> "you said 'final' night and the US just continued... you need to assume an unreliable narrator from the trump administration"; news 2026-07-21 Swiss forced-labour tariff -> "you forget to mention that there is no legal basis for these new tarifs... context... lying administration". The 'final'-class framing recurred despite the 2026-07-19 line, and the tariff reason adds a new demand: supply the missing legal context, not just attribute the loaded word. Qualifies for bounded auto-apply.

proposals.action: When a vendor's own announcement/blog is the correct primary but its page is JS-rendered and yields no fetchable text, still attach the canonical primary URL (e.g. poolside.ai/blog/<slug>) as a second link alongside the reachable secondary, rather than citing the secondary alone. The reader wants the primary reference even when the body text had to come from a secondary.
proposals.evidence: 1 downvote with a specific written reason on ai-ml 2026-07-24 Poolside Laguna S 2.1 item: "this is a secondary source!!! the poolside announcement would be the correct source". The 07-24 footer confirms the writer DID try the primary (poolside.ai) but it was JS-rendered and yielded no text, so it fell to The Decoder alone. The cheap fix is to link the primary URL even when its text is unfetchable. Not auto-applied (prompt patch, human-gated); connects to the ai-ml single-source rate of 30.6% this window, driven by The Decoder-only industry items.

proposals.action: CARRIED OVER UNAPPLIED from 2026-07-19 rm-3: in build_off_main(), compare against origin/main (the published line) rather than the local 'main' ref. The routine runs in detached HEAD after 'git pull --ff-only'; when origin/main is force-updated the local 'main' pointer stays stale, so 'git log --all --not main' reports every pulled commit as off-main.
proposals.evidence: This run reproduced the exact false positive: continuity.off_main.commits_not_on_main listed 20 commits (all 'home:'/'deck:'/'docs:' UI work provably on origin/main; remote_branches []). After 'git checkout -B main origin/main' and re-running metrics.py the count dropped to 0. The 07-19 pull was a forced update (c57bdab...ae324a6), leaving local main 34 commits behind. Guard still cries wolf every detached-HEAD run after a force-push.

proposals.action: CARRIED OVER UNAPPLIED from 2026-07-19 rm-4: do not count an analytical/prose section as empty merely because it carries no story-anchor (st-) markup. Detect emptiness by absence of body text, not absence of anchors.
proposals.evidence: This run flagged TWO false-positive empty sections in 2026-07-25-weekend.md: '🧠 Cross-cutting threads' (four substantial synthesis paragraphs, lines 14-20) and '🍎 Apple Silicon / local inference ecosystem' (a full paragraph on llama.cpp, line 140, whose single citation uses a plain markdown link with no st- anchor). Both are non-empty; the parser keys on st- anchors. The false-positive class has grown from 1 to 2 section types since the patch was proposed.
